messages:
maya_sdk: Heads-up: hitting a weird case where Authorization header disappears after a 307 redirect on Android 14 emulator. Retrofit + OkHttp combo.

jon_plat: Disappears as in not present on the redirected request to the new host?

maya_sdk: Exactly. POST to /v1/upload returns 307 -> Location to s3 proxy. OkHttp follows redirect and the new request lacks Bearer header. Works fine on older Android versions.

irene_qe: Do you have logs? Also which OkHttp version?

maya_sdk: OkHttp 4.10.0 (the SDK pins it transitively). Log snippet: 
```nI/Network: 307 Temporary Redirect for /v1/upload
I/Network: following redirect to https://s3-proxy.example.com/put/abc
I/Network: outgoing headers: Content-Type: multipart/form-data
I/Network: outgoing headers: (no Authorization)
```

paul_infra: Interesting. By default OkHttp drops Authorization on cross-host redirects for security. But you said older Android doesn't show this? Could be platform TLS/proxy weirdness or our interceptor ordering.

jon_plat: Confirming: OkHttp intentionally doesn't retain auth headers when redirecting to a different host to avoid leaking credentials. Behavior shouldn't differ by Android version ordinarily. Anything special in your interceptors (network vs application)?

maya_sdk: We use an application interceptor to add Authorization header and an authenticator to refresh tokens. The header is present before redirect, but gone after follow. On Android 13 devices the header is preserved (maybe because redirect stayed same host due to different DNS?). Emulator network mapping differs.

irene_qe: Could be the redirect response is 307 which tells client to repeat the same method and body, but OkHttp treats cross-protocol or cross-host differently. Also check followRedirects vs followSslRedirects settings.

paul_infra: Quick workaround: set client.followRedirects(false) and implement redirect handling in an interceptor where you can re-add Authorization explicitly when you trust the target host. Or implement a per-request header rewriter in network interceptor that restores Authorization for redirected calls if Location matches trusted host pattern.

jon_plat: Another safer fix: use signed short-lived upload URLs (S3 presigned) so you never forward Authorization to the storage host. If that's not possible, do manual redirect handling.

maya_sdk: For the sampleapp I added a repro under `android/samples/redirect-auth-strip` showing: (A) followRedirects=true case loses header, (B) followRedirects=false + manual follow re-add header works. Pushed a tiny test.

irene_qe: Good. Can you also check whether your application interceptor runs on the original request only? Network interceptors see the network-level redirected request and could re-inject headers. 

maya_sdk: Yep, network interceptor can see the follow-up and re-inject, but retrofit's converter for multipart has already consumed the body in some cases so replaying body is tricky. Manual handling allowed us to preserve body for small payloads in sample.

paul_infra: For docs: add note in devex "Redirects and Authorization: cross-host header stripping & mobile quirks" with recommended patterns: prefer presigned URLs, or followRedirects=false + manual handling, or network interceptor > careful body replay. Also mention emulator DNS mapping differences on Android 14.

ci-bot: CI: samples/redirect-auth-strip build queued (job #9884).

maya_sdk: Thanks. Will open the doc PR and mark as SDK guidance. If anyone has other gotchas with Android 14 redirects, ping me.
